A process that can set the turn header itself (a turn with the shell) can name a sibling running share-tier turn of the same agent, or that turn's running wake, and read its row and runs.

findings.title: A continuation rated `share` by failing closed was accepted as a share-tier turn
findings.exploit: A wake of the owner's turn is running. The read of the turn it continues fails at the moment the wake is rated, so it rates share. A request naming the wake then reads the wake's row and the owner turn's runs by id.
findings.fix: A continuation opens something only when the turn it names is read and itself rates share; one that cannot be read opens nothing.

findings.title: The no-link guard in the row match was not executed by any test
findings.exploit: With the guard deleted, a reach with no link matches every unlinked row the agent dispatched (None == None).
findings.fix: A direct test of the match with a None and an empty link against an unlinked row.

findings.title: The fan-out SQL arm's caller guard was not executed by any test
findings.exploit: With the guard deleted, a missing caller renders `source_agent_name IS NULL` and matches rows that copy the link and name no agent.
findings.fix: The database test passes a None and an empty caller against legs with no source agent.
